$comment: Pins the Godot EDITOR that ./vx setup installs into .godot-bin/. Distinct from
tools/engine-patches/engine.lock.json, which pins the export TEMPLATE a release is built from -- that
one is about what SHIPS, this one is about what a developer runs. Both must name the same engine
version; engine.lock.json's engine.version is the authority and this follows it.
WHY PIN THE EDITOR AT ALL. Every script resolves Godot through tools/lib/find-godot.sh, which probes
.godot-bin/ BEFORE PATH precisely so a clone can pin its own engine without touching the machine, and
so two clones can disagree about the version. That property is worth nothing if the thing installed
there is 'whatever was current the day someone ran setup'.
PROVENANCE OF THESE HASHES. Taken from the GitHub release API's asset digests, then CONFIRMED by
download for the platform setup was first run on -- see 'verified' per platform below. This mirrors
the standard engine.lock.json sets for itself: 'the value that causes a hard failure should be checked
against what a fetcher actually gets', not trusted from an API response. A platform marked
verified:false is pinned but not yet confirmed by download; the first setup run on that platform
confirms it, and a mismatch there is a real finding rather than a nuisance.
The MONO builds are required. The plain build cannot run C# at all, and its failure mode is a wall of
script errors that never names the cause.
ARCHITECTURE (added 2026-08-19). A platform entry is picked as platforms['<os>-<arch>'] first and
platforms['<os>'] second, and the winner's 'arch' list must CONTAIN the host architecture. That last
clause is the point: before it, a Linux machine that was not x86_64 downloaded the x86_64 zip and
found out by running it. Now it is told, with the alternative. macos carries both arches because the
asset really is universal; linux carries one because the pinned asset really is one.
An entry with a null url is a DECLARED absence, not an oversight - see linux-ppc64le. Upstream Godot
publishes no PowerPC build at all, so on that architecture there is nothing to pin and the engine has
to be compiled (tools/build-engine.sh). Saying so here is what turns 'setup failed' into 'setup told
you which command to run next'.
Godot's OWN export templates -- the set the EDITOR installs via Manage Export Templates, distinct from
the pinned custom templates in tools/engine-patches/engine.lock.json. Three of the four presets embed
a custom template and never touch these; macos-client has no custom_template/release (a declared
exception in engine.lock.json unpinned_presets) and so falls back to this set, which is why an export
on a fresh machine failed with 'No export template found' until `./vx engine --editor` existed.
Installed to the editor's per-user directory, NOT into the clone: Godot resolves them from a fixed
path it owns, so there is no repo-local option the way there is for the editor binary itself. That is
the one place vx writes outside the clone, and setup says so before doing it.
MONO build, matching the editor -- the plain templates cannot run C#.
Universal (arm64 + x86_64). The archive contains Godot_mono_macos.universal.app/; setup renames it
to Godot.app so find-godot.sh's probe path is stable across engine versions.
Note macOS quarantines downloaded bundles: the first launch may need Gatekeeper approval. setup
says so rather than stripping the attribute silently, which is a security decision that belongs to
the person running it.

linux.$comment: Archive contains a same-named directory; setup normalises the binary to .godot-bin/godot.

$comment: DECLARED ABSENCE, not a gap to fill in later. godotengine/godot publishes builds for x86_64 and
arm64 and for no PowerPC target, so there is no artifact to pin here and there will not be one
unless upstream starts producing it. The entry exists so that `vx setup` on a POWER machine reads
the reason and the alternative out of this file instead of failing on a missing key.
'godot_arch' is here because the two names disagree and both are load-bearing: the scons flag, the
engine binary's filename and a preset's binary_format/architecture all say ppc64 (Godot aliases
ppc64le to it and is little-endian only), while uname, .NET's RID and every distro say ppc64le.
The key uses the public name; anything invoking the engine build needs the other one.
The EDITOR is what this file pins, and on this architecture it is also the only thing needed for a
development loop: build it, and `vx build` / `vx test` / `vx run debug` work. Shipping a release
additionally needs an export template plus the ppc64-dotnet-rid patch - engine.lock.json, and
planning/ppc64le-port-2026-08-19.md for the whole sequence.
Carries BOTH Godot_v4.6.3-stable_mono_win64.exe and its _console.exe sibling. setup normalises them
to godot.exe and godot_console.exe, and find-godot.sh prefers the console one: the plain .exe
detaches from the terminal, so GD.Print and errors never reach a captured stdout, which every
headless and CI use in this tree depends on.
